paras: The threatened lynching of Bill Short followed the fatal shooting of Mrs. Alma Barnes, a 19-year-old widow, at a dance in Litchfield, Kansas, on the night of October 27, 1888. Short, a miner, was accused of shooting her after she refused to let him escort her home, and he was removed to Girard because of threats of lynching. No report of an attack on Short appears in the coverage, which consisted of one wire dispatch reprinted across the country.

According to a dispatch datelined Litchfield, October 28, Short was a miner and Barnes was a widow 19 years of age who left one child. The shooting occurred at a dance, and the dispatch attributed it to her refusal to allow Short to escort her home.

Barnes was shot on the night of Saturday, October 27, and died at 3 o'clock the following afternoon. The dispatch then stated that "on account of threats of lynching Short was taken to Girard." It did not say who made the threats, how many people were involved, or who moved Short. A weekly news summary in the Perrysburg Journal put it that the accused "was arrested and taken to Girard to prevent lynching."
No report of an inquest, an indictment or a trial of Short was found, and no follow-up on the threats appears in the coverage.

The Litchfield dispatch ran on October 29 in the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer, the St. Paul Daily Globe, the Fort Worth Daily Gazette, the New York Sun and the Camden Evening Telegram, among others, and in the Press and Daily Dakotaian on October 31. Several papers, including the Los Angeles Daily Herald, the Sacramento Daily Record-Union, the Silver State and the Salt Lake Herald, printed only the first two sentences and so omitted the lynching threats altogether. Weekly news summaries in Kentucky and Minnesota likewise reported the killing without mentioning lynching, while the Perrysburg Journal kept it.

Headlines framed the story as a crime of rejected courtship rather than as a mob threat: "A Brutal Murder," "Revenge of the Rejected," "A Jealous Lover" and "He Killed the Widow." The Sacramento Daily Record-Union headed its copy "A Society Event in Kansas." No paper named the race of anyone involved.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of Bill Short
bases: The only mob element reported is that Short, accused of fatally shooting Mrs. Alma Barnes, was taken to Girard 'on account of threats of lynching' (A1, A14).
Short was moved to Girard and no report says anyone attacked him (A1, A14); the coverage gives only 'threats of lynching', with no word on who made them or how many.
Every account derives from one Litchfield wire dispatch of Oct. 28 (A1), and only that dispatch and a news summary drawn from it (A14) mention the lynching threats.

accounts.label: Wire report (Litchfield, Oct. 28)
accounts.gist: Short shot Barnes at a dance after she refused his escort; she died the next afternoon; because of threats of lynching he was taken to Girard.

accounts.label: Weekly news summary
accounts.gist: Short shot and killed Barnes on the night of the 27th and was arrested and taken to Girard to prevent lynching.

framing.detail: Papers ran the dispatch under crime headlines such as 'A Brutal Murder' and 'Revenge of the Rejected'; the lynching threat was a closing clause, and several copies dropped it.

conflicts.note: Likely the same name in full form; recorded as printed.
The 'Miss' is in a shortened copy of the same wire (A2, a reprint); the full dispatch says 'Mrs.'

record_check.dossier: The threat target was Bill Short; Alma Barnes was the person he was accused of shooting, not a target of the mob.
No county is named in the coverage; only Litchfield, Kan., and Girard.
Shooting the night of Oct. 27, 1888; threats by the Oct. 28 dispatch.

record_check.record: accused of shooting Mrs. Alma Barnes
record_check.dossier: Accused of shooting and fatally wounding Mrs. Alma Barnes, who died Oct. 28, after she refused his escort home.
Short was taken to Girard because of the threats; one summary says he was arrested.
The dispatch or summaries of it ran in at least 13 white papers, Oct. 29 to Nov. 2, 1888.

info: Shooting on the night of Saturday, Oct. 27, 1888; Barnes died at 3 p.m. Oct. 28; threats and removal to Girard by the time of the Oct. 28 dispatch
At a dance in Litchfield, Kansas

Short was accused of shooting and fatally wounding Barnes because she refused to let him escort her home
